items.title: The keeper reads layouts without their version checks
items.description: The keeper accepts layouts without version checks; a future upgrade can make its decoded fields incompatible.

1.evidence: view.rs:48-54 requires shortwin ownership, matching concrete discriminator, and enough bytes for T, then returns pod_read_unaligned(body). load_with_positions:263-267,286-299,363-367 consumes GlobalConfig, Market and VenueExtras without comparing versions. MarketVault uses the same helper but has no version obligation established here. Current GlobalConfig, Market and VenueExtras have u16 version at the body start; compiled constants are 1,1,2. A same-discriminator, sufficiently sized body with another version reaches keeper interpretation.

2.evidence: No current instruction or outsider write path creates the incompatible stored version. A program-owned account cannot be rewritten by an outsider; the claimed alternative layout requires a future privileged upgrade. ProposePool owner/discriminator/PDA and CONFIG_VERSION/MARKET_VERSION guards, and parse_extras VENUE_EXTRAS_VERSION, reject unsupported inputs on-chain. This hardening class stays a lead regardless of three-agent agreement.

items.known_issue_comparison: Pass 1 records this exact keeper helper as a lead. Earlier project triage hardens VenueGuard readers (L24/L50/L61), while this helper reads GlobalConfig, Market and VenueExtras; those changes do not close this separate future-layout gap. An empty starting ledger does not establish project novelty.
items.code_smells: The decoder checks the owner, discriminator and byte length, but it omits supported-version checks.

fixes.label: Raw hardening proposal — discriminate versioned types; unapplied and uncompiled

candidate_evidence.proof: decode_zc takes the body at bytes 8..8+size_of::<T>() and returns pod_read_unaligned(body). load_with_positions uses it for GlobalConfig at line 266, Market at 289, and VenueExtras at 366 without version checks. A correctly sized GlobalConfig body with version 2 therefore decodes, although CONFIG_VERSION is 1. On-chain ApplyConfig and ProposeConfig require config.version == CONFIG_VERSION. Extras parsing likewise requires VENUE_EXTRAS_VERSION, currently 2.
candidate_evidence.guards: The keeper requires shortwin ownership, the concrete discriminator, and enough bytes. On-chain handlers reject unsupported config and market versions, so a keeper interpretation cannot bypass those checks.
candidate_evidence.impact: The keeper may plan from an unsupported layout and repeatedly submit rejected transactions after an incompatible upgrade.
candidate_evidence.limitations: No current on-chain instruction was found that writes an invalid layout version. This is a future compatibility and hardening gap.

candidate_evidence.proof: decode_zc copies the first size_of::<T>() bytes through pod_read_unaligned. load_with_positions uses it for GlobalConfig, Market, MarketVault and VenueExtras without a version test. In contrast, ProposePool explicitly requires CONFIG_VERSION and MARKET_VERSION. A future same-discriminator account of adequate length can be misread by the keeper before the program rejects its action.
candidate_evidence.guards: Owners and discriminators are checked; today's program controls account creation, and simulation limits execution effects. No current path to create an incompatible version was established.
candidate_evidence.assumption: Every program-owned account with the existing discriminator uses the compiled layout version.

candidate_evidence.proof: decode_zc accepts any shortwin-owned account whose discriminator matches T and whose data contains size_of::<T>() bytes after offset 8. It returns pod_read_unaligned without inspecting a version field. load_with_positions accepts GlobalConfig through this helper, then Market and MarketVault, and finally VenueExtras. No typed version guard follows those loads. In contrast, programs/shortwin/src/instructions/set_coverage_pause.rs:69 and :84 checks CONFIG_VERSION and MARKET_VERSION; programs/shortwin/src/venues/mod.rs:189-192 checks VENUE_EXTRAS_VERSION before the on-chain consumer uses extras. A future account with the same discriminator and sufficient bytes, but another version, therefore enters keeper decision state even when the on-chain consumer rejects it.
candidate_evidence.impact: The keeper can derive incorrect decisions or account lists during a future version transition. The current frozen state provides no outsider path to rewrite a shortwin-owned version.
candidate_evidence.limitations: This is a hardening lead, not a demonstrated present exploit. Transaction simulation and on-chain checks still restrict execution. The generic decoder alone cannot know each type's expected version.

prior_pass_comparison.assessment: Same defect re-read in frozen source; retain the exact known appendix bug-class label. Prior judgment is comparison context, not proof.

prior_issue_evidence.reason: Earlier version hardening added VenueGuard constraints to on-chain readers. The candidate concerns keeper decode_zc/load_with_positions using GlobalConfig and Market without comparing their versions: owner/discriminator/minimum length still pass. Thus the generic upgrade-compatibility pattern is known but the keeper account types and interpretation boundary are a distinct remaining extension; the on-chain VenueGuard fix does not cover it.

items.title: Correctness: Pool ranks combine LP values from different states
items.description: An LP changes liquidity after discovery, so the keeper drops eligible pools or gives other pools excessive scores.

1.evidence: CandidatePool::from_account at pool_monitor.rs:166-225 parses supported venue ownership/layout and plausible SOL side/status/nonce, then stores lp_counter. rank_keys:229-230 requests only vault and LP mint; score:238-251 requires plausible metadata, both returned accounts, vault amount bytes and a readable mint, but never refreshes the counter. A genuine pool satisfies these checks. Discovery C=1e9,S=0.5e9,R=100e9, followed by an ordinary proportional deposit to C=2e9,S=1.5e9,R=200e9, preserves locked SOL at 50e9. score:252 uses old C=1e9 with new S=1.5e9; lambda_bps checked_sub returns zero and rank:258 discards the pool. A proportional withdrawal instead overstates the share. keeper.rs:3229-3250 confirms discovery and rank reads are separate. Later genuine-account verification and transaction simulation cannot restore a discarded pool.

2.evidence: Correctness lane: source proves the wrong formula, comparison, or supported-feature behavior; no attack-state requirement is asserted.

3.evidence: Correctness lane: no attacker, financial victim, or privileged-op harm is asserted.

4.evidence: The documented locked-SOL score combines incompatible LP states and can exclude an eligible pool or displace another from the bounded candidate set. This is a source-proved formula/input mismatch. Fresh on-chain verification prevents invalid adoption; later rediscovery and direct proposals remain. No theft, profit, or stranded funds are established.

A proportional deposit doubles total liquidity: counter=2,000,000,000, supply=1,500,000,000, reserve=200,000,000,000. Locked SOL remains (2,000,000,000−1,500,000,000)*200,000,000,000/2,000,000,000=50,000,000,000. score instead evaluates lambda_bps(1,000,000,000,1,500,000,000)=0. rank retains only positive scores at pool_monitor.rs:258. Thus a valid candidate disappears before its fresh on-chain verifier runs. A withdrawal causes the converse overstatement. This does not require a counterfeit account or malicious RPC.

candidate_evidence.impact: An ordinary LP operation can remove an eligible alternate pool until the next discovery, or fill the bounded candidate set with exaggerated scores. No direct on-chain theft is established.

items.title: Correctness: Pool ranks round positive locked SOL to zero
items.description: An LP dilutes the locked share below one basis point, so the keeper excludes a pool whose locked SOL stays positive.

1.evidence: The genuine-pool owner/layout/plausibility, available-account and LP-mint guards committed for score all allow one coherent snapshot. score:252 computes floor((C-S)*10000/C)*R/10000; rank:258 removes zero before evaluate. With C=1e9,S=999950000,R=X=Y=1e15, lambda_bps is zero while (C-S)*R/C and raw locked_depth are 50e9. At P_ref=1e18 the proposal floor is 50 SOL, above 25 SOL; valid status, authorities and fee inputs pass shared eligibility. locked_depth at math/pool_select.rs:31-55 deliberately preserves raw-ratio depth, and :60-65 states that a minimum current LP-share ratio is not an eligibility requirement. This path needs no old counter or counterfeit account.

2.evidence: Correctness lane: source proves the wrong formula, comparison, or supported-feature behavior; no attack-state requirement is asserted.

3.evidence: Correctness lane: no attacker, financial victim, or privileged-op harm is asserted.

4.evidence: Whole-bps flooring discards positive eligible locked depth and can misorder other pools; rediscovery of unchanged coherent inputs does not repair the formula. The example is capital intensive and establishes a deterministic formula defect, not an economical attack or financial loss. Direct proposals and program eligibility remain.

It is a remaining distinct service site, not evidence that AIR2-09 is unfixed on-chain.

fixes.label: Calculate raw locked LP times reserve before division; unapplied and uncompiled

candidate_evidence.proof: Use one coherent snapshot with counter=1,000,000,000, supply=999,950,000 and SOL reserve=1,000,000,000,000,000. The raw locked SOL equals 50,000*1,000,000,000,000,000/1,000,000,000=50,000,000,000 (50 SOL). lambda_bps floors 0.5 bps to zero, so score returns zero. With X=Y=1,000,000,000,000,000, locked_depth instead returns 50,000,000,000; at P_ref=10^18 the window floor is 50 SOL and exceeds the 25-SOL default. The example is capital intensive but demonstrates a deterministic correctness defect without inconsistent snapshots.
candidate_evidence.guards: Genuine pool metadata and fresh LP/vault accounts do not prevent this discrepancy. The on-chain locked_depth helper deliberately uses the raw ratio and documents proportional-deposit invariance. rank removes zero scores before verification.
candidate_evidence.impact: The keeper omits positive-depth, eligible pools and can misorder other pools. The program's eligibility checks remain intact.
candidate_evidence.fix_notes: This independent diff targets the frozen source; after the stale-lp-counter fix, c must refer to the freshly parsed pool. The product fits u128 because both factors are u64.
candidate_evidence.assumption: Multiplying a whole-bps locked share by the reserve preserves the exact locked SOL score.
candidate_evidence.path: proportional unlocked liquidity dilutes the locked share → score floors lambda to whole bps → rank removes the candidate → evaluate never checks its positive locked depth.

items.title: Correctness: The keeper checks the proposal floor at the wrong price
items.description: The keeper evaluates the floor at the wrong price, so it selects a pool that the proposal instruction rejects.

1.evidence: ProposePool requires config/guard/market ownership/discriminators, PDAs and versions, market has_one mint and mint token-program owner; candidate kind must be supported, incumbent ReadSet keys valid, Pump precedence absent and the candidate venue latch clear. Use genuine distinct CPMM pools with valid config/vault/LP keys, token-program ownership, WSOL/token mint sides and vault authority, enabled swaps, elapsed open time, positive reserves and a permitted 2500-ppm fee. raydium_cpmm::verify:354-407 and raydium::check_eligible:251-283 accept these states. With no open positions, carried_fit:526-527 returns Fits. These guards are checked once for the evaluate/plan paths. evaluate:359-376 passes P_ema directly to window_floor_ok; propose_pool:314-320 passes window_price=min(P_ema,P_candidate). Take P_ema=1e18, fully locked A with X=400e9,Y=16e9,D=80e9 and floor=25e9. General eligibility at lambda_min=5000 gives 160 SOL; keeper proposal floor gives 80 SOL, actual proposal gives 16 SOL. On a Raydium incumbent of D=100e9, outside its listing window, with no positions/window and an armed failure chain, A misses the normal 25% dominance threshold 125e9 but exceeds fast_min_bps=2500 threshold 25e9. decide:299-321 returns OpenWindow. Genuine owner/layout and carried-fit checks therefore do not mask the mismatched comparison. Simulation/program rejection is the demonstrated off-chain error; rollback prevents unsafe adoption.

2.evidence: Correctness lane: source proves the wrong formula, comparison, or supported-feature behavior; no attack-state requirement is asserted.

3.evidence: Correctness lane: no attacker, financial victim, or privileged-op harm is asserted.

4.evidence: Keeper proposal evaluation disagrees with the on-chain rule and repeatedly chooses an action that is refused. A valid lower-ranked pool can be delayed; the current plan does not select it on this refusal. S3 exits and direct proposals remain. No persistent financial loss or stranded funds are proved.

items.known_issue_comparison: Pass 1 records this exact wrong argument. KI-17 at known-issues.md:93 accepts the on-chain candidate-price policy, and M4R-2 is explicit in propose_pool. That policy does not accept keeper evaluation at a different price. Prior services triage describes shared verification without identifying this argument mismatch.
items.confidence_basis: Proven correctness defect without independently proved profit, loss or stranded funds; fixed 75. Normal confidence deductions do not apply.

fixes.label: Use the proposal-specific window_price; unapplied and uncompiled
fixes.diff:
--- a/services/keeper/src/pool_monitor.rs
+++ b/services/keeper/src/pool_monitor.rs
@@ -373,7 +373,11 @@
             d: a.state.locked_depth,
             real_sol: a.state.r,
             fee_ppm: a.state.fee_ppm,
-            window_floor: pool_select::window_floor_ok(&a, params, p_ref),
+            window_floor: pool_select::window_floor_ok(
+                &a,
+                params,
+                pool_select::window_price(p_ref, &a),
+            ),
             fits: pool_select::carried_fit(market, &a, fit, p_ref, FitAt::Proposal)
                 .is_ok_and(|f| f.fits()),
         },

candidate_evidence.proof: Let P_ema=10^18 and the candidate be fully locked with X=400,000,000,000 and Y=16,000,000,000. Then D=80,000,000,000 and P_candidate=4*10^16. With pool_min_real_sol=25,000,000,000, the keeper's window_floor_ok at P_ema gives 80 SOL and true; the on-chain call at window_price gives 16 SOL and false. General eligibility still passes: at lambda_min=5,000 the eligibility reserve is 160 SOL. Take pool_d=100,000,000,000, open_positions=0, a failed incumbent with an armed fast path and no current window. D=80 billion misses the normal 25% dominance requirement (125 billion) but meets fast_min_bps=2,500 (25 billion), so decide returns OpenWindow. carried_fit returns Fits immediately with zero positions. A genuine owner/layout-verified candidate reaches the discrepancy.
candidate_evidence.guards: verify_candidate uses the correct general eligibility price; it does not apply the proposal-only floor. Simulation and the on-chain require prevent unsafe adoption, but they do not choose another candidate.
candidate_evidence.impact: The keeper repeatedly attempts a refused proposal and can delay a usable alternate pool.
candidate_evidence.assumption: A proposal checks its collection-window floor at the market EMA price alone.
candidate_evidence.path: incumbent halts at a high EMA → lower-priced alternate pool passes the keeper's floor → plan proposes it → simulation rejects PoolTooThin repeatedly.

prior_pass_comparison.assessment: Same defect re-read in frozen source; retain the exact known appendix bug-class label. Prior judgment is comparison context, not proof.

prior_issue_evidence.reason: KI-17 and M4R-2 specify the proposal floor at min(P_ema,P_cand); the execution intentionally uses P_ema. Keeper evaluate instead supplies P_ema to its proposal window_floor verdict. The prior register discusses the deliberate on-chain policy and candidate manipulation, not the keeper selecting a candidate that the same proposal refuses. This cross-component mismatch is a distinct extension; earlier shared-verifier review prose does not cover the wrong argument.

notes: The zero-position example removes carried-position uncertainty without asserting a deployed loss. Both candidates can coexist with a failed incumbent; this is a supported Raydium fast path, not the list-only zero-position branch that adopts directly.

items.title: Correctness: The keeper skips pools after a floor failure
items.description: The keeper skips viable alternatives when the deepest candidate fails the proposal floor. This path works after evaluate fixes wrong-window-floor-reference.

1.evidence: Apply the separate evaluate|wrong-window-floor-reference printed fix under the one-level bug-is-not-a-guard rule; use the committed genuine-account and no-position carried-fit guards above. On the same Raydium incumbent D=100e9, P_ema=1e18, armed failure chain, no positions/window, outside listing window: A has X=400e9,Y=16e9,D=80e9 and corrected floor=false (16 SOL); B has X=Y=D=40e9 and floor=true (40 SOL). Both pass eligibility and qualify for OpenWindow without normal dominance. plan:510-518 takes no expired-window branch; :520-528 retains both distinct non-incumbents and ranks A first. :538-539 sets PoolTooThin immediately; the alternative search :545-567 only runs for !fits, but A fits. B is skipped. Each candidate has its own min price, so the shared-price monotonicity comment is false after evaluate is repaired.

2.evidence: Correctness lane: source proves the wrong formula, comparison, or supported-feature behavior; no attack-state requirement is asserted.

3.evidence: Correctness lane: no attacker, financial victim, or privileged-op harm is asserted.

4.evidence: Repairing evaluate alone exposes this separate candidate-search defect: the keeper fails to propose accepted B after A fails its floor. The independent fix searches candidates that pass both checks. S3 exits and direct proposals remain; no profit, financial loss or irreversible lock is asserted. Fixed confidence 75 overrides ordinary masking deductions in the correctness lane.

items.title: Correctness: The keeper omits supported coin creator extras
items.description: The keeper drops every extras set with the supported coin creator placeholder, so it cannot construct those configured exit variants.

1.evidence: SetVenueExtras:107-121 requires an honest authorized Signer, current config version/PDA and extras PDA; :130-175 accepts a supported venue/ix/count and current extras version. check_entry at venues/mod.rs:297-333 accepts one SEED_PLACEHOLDER with len=PLACEHOLDER_COIN_CREATOR=4, all-zero seed bytes, zero unused seeds and nondefault external program E. Choose PumpSwap cached creator C and a derived external nonsigner PDA outside both denylists. parse_extras:177-219 verifies extras owner/PDA/version, canonical template bump/address, count, nonsigner/external ownership, denylists and writable flags; all accept the configured entry. Placeholders::key:128-137 and parse:1264-1268 resolve C from CACHED_COIN_CREATOR. Keeper resolve_entry:670-677 instead matches IDs 0..3 and returns None for 4; choice_of:704 drops the whole set and extras_candidates:738-746 omits it from current, previous and stable. With previous/stable empty, only NONE remains. keeper::attempt_trading:2861-2880 loops only this list for liquidation/expiry, so no valid configured variant is constructed.

2.evidence: Correctness lane: source proves the wrong formula, comparison, or supported-feature behavior; no attack-state requirement is asserted.

3.evidence: Correctness lane: no attacker, financial victim, or privileged-op harm is asserted.

4.evidence: Every otherwise valid PumpSwap template using the supported creator placeholder fails keeper resolution, although the on-chain feature supports it with cached data. This is a deterministic capability mismatch. A currently deployed venue requiring this extra is unproved; manual transactions, another usable set or software/configuration changes remain. No current liquidation loss or permanently stranded position is established.

candidate_evidence.assumption: The market cache cannot resolve the coin_creator placeholder.

candidate_evidence.proof: programs/shortwin/src/state/venue_extras.rs:60 defines PLACEHOLDER_COIN_CREATOR = 4. programs/shortwin/src/venues/mod.rs:297-333 accepts a SEED_PLACEHOLDER whose len is 4 and whose bytes are zero. programs/shortwin/src/instructions/set_venue_extras.rs:176-190 stores the checked set after the Signer/config authority checks at :101-117. programs/shortwin/src/venues/mod.rs:1266-1268 resolves this exact placeholder to pump_amm::cached(market, CACHED_COIN_CREATOR) for PumpSwap. items.title: A failed RPC read removes pending rank candidates
items.description: The keeper loses a pending batch after an RPC error until rediscovery. No outsider trigger or stranded funds are proved.

1.evidence: pool_monitor.rs:690-692 drains n=min(max(budget/2,1),queue.len) before the caller reads accounts. With [A,B] and a valid two-key budget, keeper.rs:3241 drains A; :3243 propagates accounts Err before finish_rank_batch:3250. RpcChain::accounts:261-289 propagates getMultipleAccounts/try_collect errors, with no returned partial batch. select_pools:3085-3098 catches and records the per-market error, then :3100-3107 retains the covered market PoolTrack. The tick continues other duties and main.rs:183-220 reuses the same keeper on later ticks. No enclosing transaction or rollback restores A. If B later scores, finish_rank_batch publishes scores without A; if the failed batch emptied the queue, the next tick skips ranking and retains old candidates (or none on first discovery).

2.evidence: The branch is reachable on an ordinary transport/RPC error; no malformed on-chain account or privileged configuration is needed. Default budget 200 permits all <=100 plausible pools to fit the failed batch; the two-pool example uses a valid configured budget of 2. discovery_due:668-677 requires the queue to be empty and the interval elapsed since last_discovery, which was stored before ranking at keeper.rs:3233. With a remaining queue, processing first continues its remaining batches; with an empty queue, rediscovery is eligible after the interval. Defaults are 10 seconds for failure/window activity and 300 seconds normally (config.rs:381-389), not a strict recovery deadline: selection allows at most two discoveries per tick, prioritizes urgency, and further RPC failures or delayed market reads can postpone it. A successful selected rediscovery calls start_ranking and restores the discovered pools. Restart creates fresh tracks and also rediscovers; no persistent source mutation is required.

3.evidence: No source trace shows an unprivileged on-chain actor can force the transport failure or an independently material consequence. The proven lost in-memory work is a recoverable operational lead, not a covered formula/comparison/layout defect or an instruction that fails for every caller. Raw item is a lead and no count-based promotion applies. Stop here.

4.evidence: Stopped after Gate 3 demotion; recovery and limitations are documented, not scored as financial harm.

items.known_issue_comparison: No matching next_rank_batch/rank_queue/RPC batch-loss issue appears in pass-1 decisions or in searches of docs/audit/ai-review*, docs/audit/known-issues.md and docs/audit/findings.md. The earlier services triage (lines 64-70) acknowledges per-market error isolation, multi-RPC reads and pool duties; it does not document discarding a drained ranking batch. KI-36 addresses crank fee-payer CU and KI-51 transaction-version/bundle deployment checks, not this queue mutation. This is new to the examined register, without a claim of global project novelty.
